Marissa — quick notes on node fleet and storage to seed the workshop: 

Node fleet (recommended starting point for ~40 qps baseline):
- Controller / infra nodes: 3 x m-class (8 vCPU, 32GB) - small fleet for
  control plane, monitoring, and NLBs
- Inference GPU pool (primary): 6 x a40 / h100-equivalent (1 GPU per
  node) - tuned for low-latency single-request throughput. Start with
  6 to hit baseline with margin; autoscale to 24 for peak bursts.
- Batch GPU pool: 4 x a10 / t4 (multi-GPU okay) — for offline batching and
  model conversions/quantization jobs
- KV cache layer: 2 x NVMe-backed nodes (no GPU) with high IOPS for
  prefix/KV caching; use local NVMe for cache and replicate via
  application-level layer.

Sizing rationale: sustained qps maps to concurrent token-generation
workers; prefer smaller GPU-per-node for predictable tail latency. We
recommend setting PodPriority and nodeSelectors to ensure inference
traffic pins to the low-latency pool.

Storage guidance:
- Model artifacts: store on a blockstore (Ceph/NetApp) mounted to nodes;
  keep hot models on local NVMe cache to reduce fetch latency.
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral on-node NVMe with periodic snapshot to
  network storage for cold-start recovery.
- Backups & retention: daily model snapshots to S3-compatible object
  store; retention policy 30–90 days depending on regulatory needs.

Operational notes:
- Image registry should be reachable from cluster; consider airgap mirror
  if policy requires.
- We should validate pod eviction pressure with synthetic traffic and
  ensure 'guaranteed' QoS for inference pods.

I'll prepare a short nodepool decision matrix for the workshop.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Planning: Clearwell on-prem K8s deployment / kickoff

Adding network / security gating items we must validate pre-workshop:

1) BGP / eBGP peering: confirm ASN and session policy. If eBGP not
   possible, confirm outbound NAT architecture and static egress IPs.
2) MTU / jumbo frames: GPUs + RDMA use cases need consistent MTU;
   confirm if spine/leaf supports 9000 bytes.
3) Traffic segregation: plan for separate VLANs for management,
   inference, storage, and egress. Document subnets and CIDR ranges.
4) Firewall & ACLs: list of IPs/ports Redwood runtime needs (K8s API,
   gRPC 443 for inference endpoints, node exporter, registry ports).
5) Monitoring & logs: agent egress destinations and retention TTLs;
   confirm whether logs may leave the VPC.
6) KMS: if Clearwell requires HSM-backed keys, note integration lead
   time and SOW impact.

Attachment: I've sketched a minimal ACL table and a revised network
diagram.

Irene
Head of Platform Security — Redwood Inference
